evidence:
MEASUREMENT GAP (why this is not a Pass). raw-evidence-index.json 'scope' states: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and target/Oracle scores are absent.' Its ten entries are scripted golden observations only (I recomputed sha256 for live-desk.cjs = 45a57f0e... and results/live-desk.json = abb06ce3..., both matching the index). qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Runtime and model evidence' requires a hash-bound runtime record for reward discrimination (mutated weak apps) before local clearance. No partial-quality app has been graded by the configured judge, so a spread is not measured. SKILL.md: 'Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass.'

SOURCE READING (what the rubric would do if the judge follows it). The structure is graded, not all-or-nothing: (1) tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the template: gates render/constraints at 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05; score.py computes a weighted mean, so reward is continuous above the floor. (2) Gates are minimal: hro_gate_render (sign-in plus workspace) and hro_gate_shared (create one requisition and one PENDING offer, read back in a fresh context; 'Approval and later actions receive separate scored credit'). They do not put advanced behaviour behind a single switch. (3) functional/judge.toml has 152 binary criteria, aggregation weighted_mean, total weight 74.0. functional/prompt.md line 15: 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failure ... Shared scenarios reduce repeated setup; they are not conjunctive scoring bundles. When a prerequisite fails, try an equivalent minimal valid UI setup', and B1/B6 repeat 'use a simpler ... eligible change set ... The failed branch's own criterion stays 0'. (4) visual is five likert-5 criteria with anchors at every level. (5) Computed functional mass by feature tier: core offer desk P1-P10 = 99 criteria, 24.3%; coordinated-change server behaviour hro_change_* = 43 criteria, 37.8%; change-desk D/L/E = 8 criteria, 36.5% (hro_desk_figures 8.1%, hro_live_stale_mark 6.8%, hro_whatif_roles 5.4%, hro_desk_remove_member 4.1%, three at 3.4%, hro_entries_reload 2.0%); R1/R2 2.7%. Reasoned ladder: blank/static shell -> gates fail -> 0; CRUD-only app -> below 0.05 floor -> 0; complete core desk with no coordinated change -> functional about 0.27; plus correct prepare/commit server contract with a submit-only form -> about 0.65; plus live desk -> up to 1.0. That is a monotone multi-step ladder consistent with the brief, whose stated ask is the change desk (instruction.md lines 1, 7, 9, 11).

CONCERN A (P2, source-level, real but bounded): the polish dimension (0.2 of reward) hangs on one precondition. All five polish criteria (polish/judge.toml: hro_pol_live_keeps_entries, hro_pol_session_resume, hro_pol_focus, hro_pol_change_recovery, hro_pol_uncertain_commit) need a working Finance coordinated-change editor with a saved preview or commit; none observes recovery quality on the ordinary offer desk. Adding functional, 0.6*(0.378+0.365)+0.2 = about 0.65 of total reward mass sits behind 'Finance can prepare a coordinated change through the UI'. Any app lacking that feature scores polish exactly 0.0 whatever its recovery quality elsewhere, so polish cannot separate such apps; they are separated only by 24-27% of functional plus visual, i.e. compressed into roughly reward 0.0-0.36.

CONCERN B (P3): 99 core criteria average about 0.25% of functional each while seven desk rows carry 34.5%; several heavy desk rows are long conjunctions of exact figures (hro_desk_figures: run-rates, both signing adjustments, both bases, headrooms, the one-cent overrun mark, a no-save read and agreement with the saved preview, all for 8.1%). One wrong figure moves functional by 0.08 while a broken core approval formula moves it by under 0.01, so run-to-run judge variance on those rows will dominate the spread among desk-capable apps. Conjunctive bundling is a listed false positive for checks 26/28/33, so I record this as a variance risk, not a defect.

What the task does well: per-actor, per-family and per-action credit is split so one failed cell does not erase siblings; negative rows require a working positive control; the functional prompt gives fallback setups so a failed transfer branch does not zero B6, receipts or authorization rows.
counterexample: Plausible weak app that is not separated: App X implements the whole base offer desk exactly (lineage, tiers, vesting, referrals, security) with entries retained after refused revisions, clear error focus and retry after a dropped request, but has no coordinated-change editor. App Y is the same core with forms that wipe every field on refusal and give no explanation. Every polish row needs a coordinated preview or commit, so both score polish 0.0; they differ only by hro_keep_revision_terms and hro_keep_rescission_date (1.35% of functional each, about 0.016 of reward). Conforming alternative at risk: an app with a correct live desk whose editor shows basis 104.02 only after a 4-second debounce loses hro_desk_figures (8.1% of functional, 'allow a few seconds' / protocol says 3 seconds) in one binary step. Neither has been run; both are reasoned from source.
suggested_fix: Before clearance, record the required reward-discrimination runs with the configured judge on at least three mutated apps (core-only, core plus submit-only coordinated change, full golden) and confirm their rewards are distinct and ordered. If the owner wants polish to discriminate below the coordinated-change tier, re-home one recovery observation that needs only the ordinary offer desk (for example the retained-revision-terms row) into polish within existing public requirements; do not touch scoring.toml, score.py or test.sh.
